    Sutton Council names St George as the developer behind the permission, while the homes are sold as Berkeley. Which company signs my contract and holds the freehold, and what is its Companies House number?

Start here: the questions that matter most

Eight to put first. The full wording, the closing test and a place to track each are in "Every question, by stage".

  1. Q1 Ask the legal team, before booking

    Sutton Council names St George as the developer behind the permission, while the homes are sold as Berkeley. Which company signs my contract and holds the freehold, and what is its Companies House number?

    Your contract is enforceable against the company that signs it, not the brand.

  2. Q2 Ask the site and engineering team, before booking

    The scheme has eight buildings of 6 to 21 storeys. Is The Kensington's building a higher-risk building (18 metres or seven storeys), and if so, has the Building Safety Regulator approved Gateway 2 for it? Please share the approval notice and its date.

    For a higher-risk building, construction may not start before Gateway 2 approval and nobody may move in before a Gateway 3 completion certificate. Delays at either gateway move your completion date.

  3. Q3 Ask the site and engineering team, before booking

    Piling began on 16 July 2026. Was that work covered by an approved building control application, or was the work split into stages with separate approvals?

    Starting higher-risk building work without approval is an offence, and enforcement can halt the site.

  4. Q4 Ask the legal team, before signing

    Berkeley says the first homes complete from 2028; an agent says Q4 2028 to Q1 2029. What completion date, long-stop date and right to rescind will my contract contain?

    Off-plan contracts in England usually give the developer a long-stop date; until then you may have no remedy for delay.

  5. Q5 Ask the legal team, before signing

    Where will my deposit be held: by your solicitors as stakeholder, or released to the developer? Is it protected if the developer cannot complete?

    A deposit released to the developer before completion is at risk if the company fails.

  6. Q6 Ask the legal team, before signing

    Which new-home warranty covers my apartment (for example NHBC or Premier), for how long, and from what date? Please share the provider and the policy summary.

    A ten-year structural warranty is what most lenders require and what protects you from defects after the first years.

  7. Q7 Ask the legal team, before signing

    What are the lease terms: length, ground rent, service charge budget for the first year, reserve fund, and any estate charge for the 1.1-acre park and public realm? Who is the management company?

    Service and estate charges on large mixed schemes can rise sharply; the first-year budget and how costs are shared with 1,014 homes matter.

  8. Q8 Ask the sales team, before signing

    How is the apartment heated: by its own system or a shared heat network? If shared, what are the standing charges, who supplies the heat, and is the network covered by heat network regulation?

    Heat network customers cannot switch supplier, so the terms decide what you pay for years.

Building safety, possible link

At least some buildings at Sutton Garden Square are likely to be higher-risk buildings (the scheme ranges from 6 to 21 storeys). If The Kensington's building is one, its timeline depends on two approvals from the Building Safety Regulator, before work and before occupation, which developers in England have reported as a common source of delay.

  1. The permission covers eight buildings of 6 to 21 storeys sutton.gov.uk / w/plans-for-new-homes-at-key-town-centre-site-approved
  2. Buildings of 18 metres or seven storeys need Gateway 2 approval before work and a Gateway 3 certificate before occupation gov.uk / building-safety-bill-factsheets/building-control-regime…
